summary: The neutral stance (0.55 confidence, as quoted in the PM's reasoning in close.json) was consistent with the first trading day but is barely tested by it. SPY gained 0.335% (spy_value 602.01 on a 600 start). The agent book finished at 599.96 (-0.007%), with only about 39% invested after four fills (DPZ, IDXX, VOO, WMT) and the rest in cash. The defensive tilts (favor Staples/Health Care, avoid Tech/Industrials per the PM's quotes) were neutral to slightly positive on the day: DPZ +3.6% and VOO +0.4% on change_today, IDXX +0.4%, WMT -0.5%. Day P/L was -0.04. The book trailed SPY by about 0.34 points because it held mostly cash in a rising market, not because the calls were wrong. One day is too short to grade a stance.
update: No change to the stance from one day's evidence. Caveats: (1) inputs/learning.json does not exist in the run directory, so no lessons or graded_calls were applied; the Reviewer pipeline should confirm whether this is expected on day one. (3) Watch items carried forward: the VOO invalidation (SPY close below ~736.8, or HYG 21d below -3%) is the closest checkable trigger. HYG was at -1.73% 21d and -1.37% from its 200-day at the 10-19 packet, so credit is the soft spot to monitor. The 5-day tech drop (XLK -5.3%, QQQ -3.7%) and small-cap weakness (IWM -4.5% 21d, below its 200-day) did not break the regime (SPY +6.11% over its 200-day). If the mega-cap earnings pass and SPY holds, the stance could move toward risk-on; if HYG breaks or SPY nears 736.8, it moves toward risk-off.
